scenes.heading: Coenzymes
scenes.sub: The little helpers that keep pathways running
scenes.say: Cells don't do big reactions in one jump. They use biochemical pathways, and many of the enzymes need tiny helpers called coenzymes. Understanding them is the key to photosynthesis and respiration.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Shuttle buses carry fans to the stadium, then return empty
scenes.science: NAD⁺ loads up as NADH, drops off at the ETC, returns as NAD⁺
scenes.breaks: buses travel far, but coenzymes diffuse short distances, and what they carry is chemically bonded to them.
scenes.say: Think of game-day shuttle buses. N A D plus is an empty bus. It picks up electrons and a proton, becoming loaded NADH, drops them at the electron transport chain, and comes back empty for more. If the buses never come back, loading has to stop.
scenes.caption: Think of game-day shuttle buses. NAD⁺ is an empty bus. It picks up electrons and a proton, becoming loaded NADH, drops them at the electron transport chain, and comes back empty for more. If the buses never come back, loading has to stop.

scenes.heading: Biochemical pathways
points: Product of one step = substrate of the next
Each step has its own specific enzyme
Small steps capture energy as ATP
One enzyme can control the whole pathway
scenes.say: In a pathway, the product of one step is the substrate for the next, and each step has its own enzyme. Small steps let the cell capture energy in usable packets of ATP, instead of losing it as heat. And the cell can control the whole pathway by regulating one enzyme.

scenes.heading: Cofactors vs coenzymes
scenes.say: A cofactor is any non-protein helper for an enzyme. Metal ions like magnesium are inorganic cofactors. Coenzymes are the organic ones, like ATP and NAD plus. They carry things between reactions and get reused. So all coenzymes are cofactors, but not all cofactors are coenzymes.
scenes.caption: A cofactor is any non-protein helper for an enzyme. Metal ions like Mg²⁺ are inorganic cofactors. Coenzymes are the organic ones, like ATP and NAD⁺. They carry things between reactions and get reused. So all coenzymes are cofactors, but not all cofactors are coenzymes.

scenes.heading: Loaded and unloaded
scenes.say: Learn these four pairs. ADP plus phosphate loads up as ATP, carrying energy. NAD plus becomes NADH in respiration. FAD becomes FADH two in the Krebs cycle. And NADP plus becomes NADPH in photosynthesis. P for photosynthesis!
scenes.caption: Learn these four pairs. ADP + Pi loads up as ATP, carrying energy. NAD⁺ becomes NADH in respiration. FAD becomes FADH₂ in the Krebs cycle. And NADP⁺ becomes NADPH in photosynthesis. P for photosynthesis!

scenes.heading: ATP releases energy
scenes.say: Removing ATP's last phosphate releases energy for work like muscle contraction. ATP is pocket money, not savings. Glucose, starch and fat are the long-term stores.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: W → X → Y → Z. A mutant can't make enzyme 2 (X → Y). What happens to W, X, Y and Z?
lines: Enzyme 1 works: W still becomes X
No Y made, so no Z either
Answer: X piles up; Y and Z absent
scenes.say: A mutant can't make enzyme two, which turns X into Y. W still becomes X, but X can't go any further, so X builds up. No Y is made, so no Z either. Like cars before a closed bridge.

points: Coenzymes are loaded, unloaded and reused
NADH, NADPH, FADH₂ carry electrons + protons
scenes.say: Quick recap. Pathways are chains of enzyme steps. Coenzymes are organic cofactors that get loaded, unloaded and reused. ATP carries energy, while NADH, NADPH and FADH two carry electrons and protons. Now try the practice questions!
